free_tier.stated: 'New workspaces get $30 of free credit, once per person ... and the tour starts a box on it with no card. It does not refill.' While on the credit alone: sizes Nano to Small only, one box at a time, no process at full CPU for more than 30 minutes.
free_tier.notes: Smallest grant in this category, but the only one whose meters let a single credit run a box for multiple months.

per_object_cap.stated: On the free credit 'Nano, Micro, Extra Small, or Small only'; Medium and larger answer `409 tier_unavailable`. A Nano is 2 vCPU / 2 GB / 40 GB at USD 0.014 an hour awake.
per_object_cap.notes: A Small is 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 300 GB at USD 0.137 an hour, which burns the whole USD 30 in nine days.

retention.stated: a paused sandbox is deleted 30 days after its last use on the free tier; a stopped box's disk is kept and billed at USD 0.0001 per GB-hour while asleep

egress.terms: outbound traffic is not filtered; no allowance or per-GB price is published

record.interface_detail: SSH to the box (plain ssh or prized ssh); the prized CLI (macOS, Linux, Windows); an HTTP API for boxes and sandboxes; a browser dashboard
record.tooling: SSH to a box with a standard client or the prized CLI; a CLI and an HTTP API drive boxes and sandboxes

limits.value: USD 30 one-time free credit, once per person
one box at a time on the credit
no process at full CPU for more than 30 minutes on the credit

record.limits_note: The 30-minute full-CPU rule can pause the workspace and answer 409 workspace_held on the next create or wake; it is a use cap that no other provider here imposes.

identity_cost.detail: 'the tour starts a box on it with no card' and the credit is once per person by email or by Google or GitHub account. No card, no phone, no ID at signup; paid plans use Stripe Checkout, cards only.

record.reliability_note: On the credit a box auto-pauses itself after 2 hours idle unless the window is changed or switched off per box; it never pauses in its first 24 hours.
record.confidence_note: Every number is from the billing page read. Not observed: whether the 30-minute CPU rule is enforced by cgroup throttling or by pausing, which decides whether a long build is slowed or killed.

# Billing > How a monthly plan ($10 to $1,000, or sized to your boxes past that) becomes credit, what boxes cost by the hour, and what happens when the credit runs out.

evidence.proved: a paused free-tier sandbox is deleted after 30 days of no use
evidence.quote: on the free tier it is deleted 30 days after its last use

evidence.proved: SSH is the documented way to work on a box
evidence.quote: You edit and run everything on the box over SSH.

evidence.proved: the free credit is USD 30 once per person and needs no card
evidence.quote: New workspaces get $30 of free credit, once per person, as the owner walks through onboarding or first signs in with `prized login` through the browser (an account a coding agent made gets it, or not, when its code is checked: [Agent sign-in](https://prized.dev/docs/agent-sign-in#boxes-and-billing)); it spends like paid credit, and the tour starts a box on it with no card. It does not refill: at zero, boxes pause ([Running out](#running-out)) and the dashboard opens on the plan picker. Choosing a plan keeps what is left, and the first cycle's credit lands at once.

evidence.proved: the credit is once per email or Google or GitHub account and needs no card
evidence.quote: A workspace whose owner already took the free credit, on the same email address or the same Google or GitHub account, gets none, including after [erasing](https://prized.dev/docs/data-retention#closing-a-workspace) the first workspace.
You edit and run everything on the box over SSH.

evidence.proved: the free-tier sandbox shape and 60-minute run cap are restated
evidence.quote: Sandboxes on the free credit run within the [free tier](https://prized.dev/docs/sandboxes#free-tier): up to 10 at once, each up to 2 vCPU, 4 GB of memory and 60 minutes.

record.notes: USD 30 / USD 0.014 = 2,143 hours, which is 89 days of a 2 vCPU / 2 GB box with no card. The page's own claim of 'about three months on a Nano' matches. This is the longest no-card calendar coverage in this category and it is a real VM, not a sandbox, but a 2 vCPU / 2 GB box is also the smallest shape any row here offers for a full month.

extras.billing_model: per-second while awake, per GB-hour while asleep

session_cap.note: 2-hour idle auto-pause by default on the credit; can be changed per box or switched off

extras.credit_expiry: does not refill; rollover on a paid plan is two months

record.binding_note: The 30-minute full-CPU rule is what fails first for any real build; the credit itself is generous at the Nano size.
